ledger.note: 30 May 1967: Biafra declares independence. Infobox 'Independence declared: 30 May 1967'; the Civil War page: 'Ojukwu declared independence and renamed the entire Eastern Region "the Republic of Biafra"'. The region is the page's; the admin-1 mapping is the researcher's.

ledger.note: August 1967: Biafra invades the Mid-West. 'On 9 August, Biafran forces crossed their western border and the Niger river into the Mid-Western state of Nigeria'; the Biafra page: 'This led to the creation of the Republic of Benin, a short lived puppet-state.' The year is read from the page's 1967 sequence.

region.text: the Mid-Western state (modern Edo and Delta: the researcher's mapping)

ledger.note: 22 September 1967: the Mid-West is lost. 'Benin City was retaken by the Nigerians on 22 September'; the Biafran administrator's 'Republic of Benin', declared 19 September, 'ceased to exist the next day'.

region.text: Enugu, taken by the Nigerian 1st Division

ledger.note: 4 October 1967: Enugu falls. 'On 4 October, the Nigerian 1st Division captured Enugu.' The year follows from the page's 12 September 1967 sentence on the plan to take it.

October 1967: the Biafran government moves from Enugu to Umuahia. After Enugu fell, 'Ojukwu relocated his government without difficulty to Umuahia, a city positioned deep within traditional Igbo territory.' The infobox gives Umuahia for 1967-1969.
19 May 1968: Port Harcourt falls. 'On 19 May 1968 Port Harcourt was captured.'
1969: the capital moves to Owerri. Infobox: Owerri (1969-1970); the page gives no day or month and no account of the loss of Umuahia.
1970: the capital is Awka. Infobox: Awka (1970); Ojukwu 'fled to Ivory Coast on 8 January 1970'.

wars.outcome: Nigerian victory on 15 January 1970: Biafra and the short-lived Republic of Benin dissolved and Nigeria was reunified.
wars.note: Fronts: Mid-West 9 August - 22 September 1967; Enugu 4 October 1967; Port Harcourt 19 May 1968. 'Only five countries (Tanzania, Gabon, Ivory Coast, Zambia, and Haiti) officially recognised the new republic'; Gabon and Ivory Coast did so in May 1968.

certainty.note: A secessionist state at war: the claimed Eastern Region is a colonial-era province, but the territory actually held changed with the front, which the pages date only for Enugu (4 October 1967) and Port Harcourt (19 May 1968).

notes: Written by the batch af-08-h (the brief lets it add rebel states that bear on its states); the scope also names Biafra for the additions batch af-08-x, whose agent should keep this file or merge into it. Budget: 2 pages. The territory held after Enugu and Port Harcourt (Calabar, Aba, Umuahia, Owerri, the Uli airstrip) is not dated by the pages opened; a gap-filler should open the Biafra campaign articles. The Mid-West 'Republic of Benin' (19-20 September 1967) is recorded as an occupation, not a separate state. Regions: the Eastern Region is a union of nine modern admin-1 states; Enugu and Port Harcourt are 50 km radii. Biafra's recognition by Gabon and Ivory Coast in May 1968 is in the Civil War page; the republic-of-cote-d-ivoire and gabon dossiers mention it only in notes. Counterpart: federal-republic-of-nigeria carries the matching loss, occupation and gain events.
